User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the BrandNarrator application.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

lastLogin.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user logged in.

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Represents a user's subscription plan and payment status.

planName.description: Name of the subscription plan (e.g., Basic, Premium).

paymentMethod.description: Payment method used for the subscription (e.g., credit card, crypto).

PaymentTransaction.title: PaymentTransaction
PaymentTransaction.description: Represents a payment transaction processed via NOWPayments.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment transaction.

paymentId.description: The payment ID returned by NOWPayments.

payinAddress.description: The cryptocurrency address where the payment was sent.

payoutAddress.description: The cryptocurrency address where the payment was sent.

paymentStatus.description: The status of the payment (e.g., confirmed, sending, waiting, finished, failed, refunded).

paymentCurrency.description: The cryptocurrency or fiat currency used for payment.

paymentAmount.description: The amount paid in the payment currency.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the payment transaction was created.

BrandStory.title: BrandStory
BrandStory.description: Represents the generated brand story for a user's startup.

id.description: Unique identifier for the brand story.

content.description: The generated narrative content of the brand story.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the brand story was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the brand story was last updated.

SocialMediaPost.title: SocialMediaPost
SocialMediaPost.description: Represents a scheduled social media post.

id.description: Unique identifier for the social media post.

platform.description: The social media platform for the post (e.g., Facebook, Twitter, Instagram).

content.description: The content of the social media post.

scheduledTime.description: Date and time when the post is scheduled to be published.

status.description: Status of the post (e.g., scheduled, published, failed).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the social media post was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the social media post was last updated.

AIPrompt.title: AIPrompt
AIPrompt.description: Represents an AI-optimized prompt generated for different AI platforms.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AI prompt.

platform.description: The AI platform for which the prompt is designed (e.g., GPT-3, Bard).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the AI prompt was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the AI prompt was last updated.

ContentAnalytic.title: ContentAnalytic
ContentAnalytic.description: Represents the analytics data for a specific social media post.

id.description: Unique identifier for the content analytics.

impressions.description: Number of impressions the post received.

clicks.description: Number of clicks the post received.

likes.description: Number of likes the post received.

shares.description: Number of shares the post received.

comments.description: Number of comments the post received.

engagementRate.description: The calculated engagement rate of the post.

dateAnalyzed.description: Timestamp indicating when the analytics data was captured.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. User data and their associated brand stories, social media posts, AI prompts, content analytics, subscriptions, and payment transactions are organized in a hierarchical manner under the `/users/{userId}` collection. This approach provides clear ownership and simplifies security rules. Subscriptions and payment transactions are separated out into dedicated subcollections to facilitate secure querying and management of subscription statuses and payment histories. This design avoids the use of `get()` calls in security rules, promoting atomic operations and simplifies debugging. The structure also explicitly addresses the need for easy listing of user-owned entities, thus fulfilling the QAPs requirement. Denormalization is not explicitly required as all data is user-owned and path-based. This inherently provides authorization independence. The structure also supports invariants such as ownership (via the path) and timestamps.
